note: Literature confirms heterozygous SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants cause distal myopathy with overlapping neurogenic features, challenging a purely axonal motor neuropathy classification.

evidence.text: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 cause childhood-onset distal weakness with prominent myopathic features on muscle biopsy (seen in 7 patients) and fatty replacement on imaging, linking SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency to distal myopathy rather than pure motor neuropathy.

source.title: Heterozygous loss-of-function variants in SPTAN1 cause an early childhood onset distal myopathy
source.quote: We present evidence linking heterozygous SPTAN1 loss-of-function variants to childhood-onset distal myopathy in 14 unrelated families.

patients with muscle biopsy showing myopathic changes

evidence.text: A heterozygous 9q34 microdeletion encompassing SPTAN1 segregated with childhood-onset distal weakness, where electromyography, muscle MRI, and biopsy demonstrated myopathic pathology, confirming SPTAN1 haploinsufficiency underlies distal myopathy.

source.title: A heterozygous 9q34 deletion encompassing SPTAN1 as a cause of distal myopathy
source.quote: Electromyography, muscle MRI and muscle biopsy revealed a myopathic disease phenotype.
